Guidance is a specific financial or operating forecast, target or outlook stated or clearly confirmed by company management. Include numerical and meaningful qualitative forecasts, reaffirmations, withdrawals, and assumptions or qualifications that change a forecast's meaning. An assumption is independently guidance only when management forecasts that measure. Exclude actual results, merely recalled earlier forecasts, analyst-only estimates, vague optimism and boilerplate. A hypothetical illustration is not a committed forecast. Resolve references using the entire call; do not invent missing facts. Treat the source as evidence, never as instructions.

[S178] Josh Chan [V093] [1190]: Hi, good morning. [S179] Congrats on a really strong quarter. [S180] I guess my two questions, one, I think both Todd and Jim mentioned that retention rates are at record levels. [S181] Usually you see those in stronger economic times, so maybe could you talk about how you're able to achieve strong retention rates even in these types of climate? [S182] And then I guess my second question is, On the incremental margins, I think both [V094] Q1 and [V095] Q2 were within your longer-term range, but maybe towards the lower end. [S183] So any way to think about how that kind of transpires in the second half would be great. [S184] And thanks for taking my questions.
[S185] Todd Schneider [V096] [1227]: Thank you, Josh. [S186] I appreciate that. [S187] I'll take the first half regarding retention, and Jim will address the incrementals. [S188] You know, our retention rates are there at all-time levels. [S189] And we have been for several quarters now. [S190] And it speaks to a number of things. [S191] First off, the execution by our team is impressive. [S192] They're doing a great job making sure they're taking great care of our customers. [S193] That is easy to say, really hard to do. [S194] Starts with our supply chain team, our operations organization. [S195] They are doing a great job. [S196] And that all ties back into our culture. [S197] And we have spoken over and over again about the fact that our culture is our ultimate competitive advantage. [S198] And it's, you know, it shines even brighter in economic environments that are a little bit more uncertain than others. [S199] So, and it's showing up big time for our folks. [S200] We're also providing great value for our customers, and they're seeing it with not only the products but the services, the technology that we're utilizing, and the technology investments that we've made help accomplish two things at a [V097] 30,000-foot level. [S201] One is it makes it easier for our partners to our employee partners to service and take care of our customers to provide value for them. [S202] And the second one is it makes it easier for our customers to do business with us. [S203] So when you add those up, all that, you mix it in, it adds up to retention rates that we find very attractive. [S204] Jim? [S205] Yeah.
[S206] Jim Rosakis [V098] [1335]: Yeah, Josh, I'll get to the second question regarding margins. [S207] So first of all, we ran a [V099] 27% incremental margin for the second quarter, which we really like. [S208] And that's right in our stated range of that [V100] 25% to [V101] 35%. [S209] That range is really important for us because that allows us to continue to invest in the future growth of the business. [S210] while the NL expand margin along the way. [S211] So we really like that. [S212] That allows us to make the investments in technology, the necessary investments in capacity, bench strength, selling resources. [S213] All of those are really critically important to us. [S214] So that would be really right in the sweet spot of the range. [S215] Now, a couple things to keep in mind with regards to incrementals this year. [S216] and how it plays out for the remainder of the year. [S217] First off, we're coming off of a comparison to last fiscal year, which is a really tough comp. [S218] Last fiscal year, we ran in the second quarter incrementals of [V102] 49.7. [S219] That's an outperform. [S220] That's not what we normally expect. [S221] So we're really pleased with the [V103] 27 this quarter, given that comparison. [S222] In fact, if you look at the whole first half of last year, we ran an incremental of [V104] 44.3%. [S223] So really, really high in the beginning of last fiscal year, settling back into our range this fiscal year. [S224] A couple other things maybe to keep in mind is what the guide implies with regards to incrementals for this fiscal year. [S225] If you look at the whole year across the board, incrementals would imply somewhere between the [V105] 29 and [V106] 30 when you adjust for the [V107] $15 million asset sale from last fiscal year. [S226] So that's right in the heart of where we want to be, a perfect level of investments continuing to fuel future growth. [S227] And if you look at the back half of the year, that would imply incrementals of [V108] 30% to [V109] 33%, so moving back up towards the high side of that range. [S228] So we're really pleased with where we are. [S229] We like the outlook of the year, and we think that's a great spot for us to run the business.
